symbols.name: guard width
symbols.meaning: The count of extra fractional and integer bits reserved per real component, so $p+\Delta$ fractional bits are kept.
symbols.quote: The guard-width bound makes every intermediate coefficient of one [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-butterfly-layer.md) exact, by reserving an explicit count $\Delta$ of extra fractional and integer bits per real component, so that a single final truncation suffices.

symbols.name: first input value
symbols.meaning: The first of the two complex input values of the two-point map.
symbols.quote: The two-point map sends two complex input values $u,v$ (these letters change meaning here) to $((u+v)/2,\ (u-v)/2)$.

symbols.name: second input value
symbols.meaning: The second of the two complex input values of the two-point map.
symbols.quote: The two-point map sends two complex input values $u,v$ (these letters change meaning here) to $((u+v)/2,\ (u-v)/2)$.

symbols.name: value depth
symbols.meaning: The number of arithmetic operations on a chain computing a value from an input.
symbols.quote: Let $\ell$ be the depth of a value, the number of operations on a chain that follows an operand from an input into it.

symbols.name: group size
symbols.meaning: The number of selected axes in a group that the recursion splits.
symbols.quote: a group of $e$ selected axes splits into $s$ calls on groups of $e/m$ axes

symbols.name: operation bound
symbols.meaning: An upper bound on the number of operations on any chain within a group of e axes.
symbols.quote: Let $A(e)$ bound the operations on any chain within such a group.

symbols.name: division factor
symbols.meaning: The factor by which a call of the complex phase network divides the number of axes.
symbols.quote: a group of $e$ selected axes splits into $s$ calls on groups of $e/m$ axes, where $W$ is the wire count, $s$ the smaller-call count, and $m$ the factor by which a call divides the axis count (the letter $m$ changes meaning here).

symbols.name: gate constant
symbols.meaning: The constant $64(W+m+1)^3$ bounding the operations for gates and corrections at one node.
symbols.quote: plus at most $\eta=64(W+m+1)^3$ operations for the gates at the node

symbols.name: operation growth factor
symbols.meaning: The constant $s+\eta$ by which each recursion level multiplies a bound.

symbols.name: depth constant
symbols.meaning: The constant $128m\beta^2$ in the depth bound $C_0d^{C_1}$.
symbols.quote: Let $C_0=128m\beta^2$ and $C_1=\max\{20,\nu+3\}$, so every value has $\ell\le C_0d^{C_1}$.

symbols.name: depth exponent
symbols.meaning: The constant $\max\{20,\nu+3\}$ in the depth bound $C_0d^{C_1}$.
symbols.quote: Let $C_0=128m\beta^2$ and $C_1=\max\{20,\nu+3\}$, so every value has $\ell\le C_0d^{C_1}$.

relations.quote: The guard-width bound makes every intermediate coefficient of one [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-butterfly-layer.md) exact, by reserving an explicit count $\Delta$ of extra fractional and integer bits per real component, so that a single final truncation suffices.
Intermediate values are exact [Gaussian dyadics](gaussian-dyadics.md), so the bound must limit the denominators of the values.
The bound must allow for operators that are not [linear contractions](linear-contraction.md), meaning linear maps that can increase the largest modulus of a vector.
The bound applies to the output of the [tensor product](tensor-product.md) of $D$ copies of the map.
The growth of $d$ is stated with [Big-Theta notation](big-theta-notation.md): $d=\Theta(p^{\varepsilon})$ means $d$ lies between two constant multiples of $p^{\varepsilon}$ for large $p$.
